free_tier.stated: Start your 30-day Snowflake trial with USD 400 in free credits. The documentation states: 'To sign up for a trial account, all you need is a valid email address; no payment information or other qualifying information is required.' AI features are disabled on a self-service trial account until a credit card is added.

egress.terms: Per-byte egress fee for transfers into a different region or cloud platform, with transfers inside the same region free and no ingress fee; the per-byte rate depends on the hosting region and is on the separate pricing guide, not read.

record.interface_detail: Snowflake CLI, an open-source command line client for SQL execution and for Snowpark, Streamlit and Native App objects, over a configured connection; SnowSQL is the legacy command line client; documented at docs.snowflake.com
record.tooling: Snowflake CLI (open source, the preferred client) and SnowSQL (legacy client)
record.chaining: USD 400 of Snowflake credit is a genuine warehouse for a month and is the standard route to loading a large public dataset once; nothing about it composes, because both the credit and the access end on the same day.
record.limits_note: at USD 2 a credit on AWS US East Standard and 1 credit an hour for an X-Small Gen1 warehouse, the USD 400 buys 200 warehouse-hours, which is 8.3 days of continuous running
record.binding_note: the 30-day clock ends the USD 400 before any usage ceiling is reached

card.summary: No byte quota. A $400 credit balance and a 30-day clock, whichever ends first. 'The trial continues for 30 days (from the sign-up date) or until you've deple...

free_tier.stated: No byte quota. A $400 credit balance and a 30-day clock, whichever ends first. 'The trial continues for 30 days (from the sign-up date) or until you've depleted your free usage balance.' Storage accrues cost against that balance at standard rates (~$40/TB/month per the documented Standard rate). So the nominal free storage is whatever the credit buys after compute: at $40/TB/mo, $400 buys 10 TB-months, i.e. 10 TB for one month or 1 TB for ten.

egress.terms: Not free. Snowflake bills egress/transfer separately and the trial credit is consumed by it.

record.tooling: Excellent: PUT to an internal stage, full SQL, Snowflake SDKs, and external stages pointing at your own S3/Azure/GCS. Programmatically the best of the warehouse entrants.
record.chaining: One trial per email; trials cannot be chained legitimately because the account is suspended at day 30. 'At the end of the trial, the account is suspended. You can still log into a suspended account, but you cannot use any features, such as … loading data.'.
record.limits_note: retention-clamped and hard-capped by design. Data is NOT deleted on suspension but is also not retrievable, which is worse than deletion for the purpose of treating it as storage. Identity is email only, which is the one thing in its favour.
record.reliability_note: Suspension at day 30 makes this a 30-day buffer, not storage. Any chunked-object scheme built on it would need a full re-upload cycle monthly.
